newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian central banker talks damp currency market.
newsitem.headline: Asian central banker talks damp currency market.

text.p: Southeast Asian currencies were on slightly firmer footing on Friday morning as the market paused from its recent frantic selling just in case an Asian central bankers meeting in Shanghai sprang a surprise.
The one-day meeting was expected to yield little more than warnings against currency speculation and talk of cooperation, but dealers said the market was taking nothing for granted.
"The market is cautious in case anything happens. I would advise customers to trim down their positions or just square up," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
Dealers said there were still some fears of concerted intervention to counter the recent series of attacks on regional currencies, but most were unconvinced.
"In general, it looks like the central banks have decided not to waste foreign exchange reserves intervening against market forces," a senior dealer at another European bank said.
The Thai baht remained weak as companies sought the dollar to meet payments and the market worried about the battered financial sector.
But dealers said trade was calmer than in recent days and the baht stayed above the low of 32.70 to the dollar it hit on Thursday.
Some Bangkok dealers said they saw strong support for the baht around the 32.30 level, but they were not sure whether the central bank had intervened in the market.
"The market was quite calm this morning with only small buying. There was light commercial demand and the baht moved in a very tight band," a foreign bank dealer said.
The Singapore dollar bounced back sharply from a morning low of 1.4765 at the open, prompting talk of possible intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).
But most dealers attributed the move to nervous profit-taking by a market that had bought up the U.S. dollar aggressively in the last two days.
"The MAS wouldn't come in at this level, especially as the Finance Minister has said market forces should determine the exchange rate," said one.

Finance Minister Richard Hu told parliament on Wednesday Singapore's exchange rate was determined by market demand and it would continue to be managed on a trade-weighted basis with a medium-term perspective.
The Singapore dollar was expected to trade a 1.4700-1.4760 range for the day. It was at 1.4729/39 at 0440 GMT.
Selling of the Malaysian ringgit subsided but the currency's recovery was blocked around the 2.64 level to the dollar and dealers continued to predict more weakness.
"I don't think dollar/ringgit has seen a top yet. It should go to 2.70 eventually and the recent low of 2.6180/2.6200 should hold," a Singapore-based dealer said.
"The market is very quiet today, kind of in a squarish mode. They are probably waiting to see if any concrete measures emerge from Shanghai," said another Singapore dealer.
The Indonesian rupiah remained depressed below the 2,600 level to the dollar, but dealers said activity had slowed.
"It's still a regional factor. Fund managers who are playing in Jakarta have also exposures in Thailand and the ringgit. Once they move, all those currencies are affected," one said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,610/20 at 0440 GMT compared with an opening of 2,601/09.
The Philippine central bank sold dollars in the face of heavy commercial demand, helping stem the peso's fall.
The Hong Kong dollar calmed down, but tension lingered after forwards shot up on Thursday, sparking fears of a speculative attack on Asia's most strongly pegged currency.
Hong Kong Monetary Authority released figures after the market closed on Thursday, showing it held HK$569 billion at June 30, up 6.4 percent from December 31, 1996.
Analysts saw the move as aimed at scaring off speculators.
